title: Chapter 1: Today is a Good Day to Throw My Life Away 3
content: I understood, but my feet wouldn't stop. While healing the various damages with recovery magic, I kept running. Behind my closed eyelids, my crushed eyeballs healed.

When my vision returned, the first thing I saw was the masked attacker, frozen in shock just a breath away. What the hell? Is this the first time I've encountered an idiot who charges through an explosion? It’s my first time too.
I swung my sword, aiming for the attacker’s neck.
However, the damage from the explosion lingered more than I expected. My sword wavered as my organs were scraped by ribs that hadn’t properly reattached.
The attacker, with a voice muffled by the mask, spat curses while deflecting my sword with a dagger.
I cursed inwardly for not taking them down in the first move against someone who primarily fought with magic. Could it be that I hesitated to kill someone with my own sword at this late stage?
I’ll state it clearly: if you’re a noble, you will inevitably kill someone someday.
Whether directly or indirectly, I don’t know, but we nobles will definitely kill someone eventually.
It’s just a matter of awareness, and my “first time” will be for the woman I love.
Bring it on, I’m ready.
Just then, I remembered that I had just smashed someone’s head with the dagger I threw earlier.
Alright, die!
I chased after the attacker, who was trying to create some distance.

It seemed the mask was a type of magic tool, as the attacker waved their left hand while muttering something in a voice that didn’t reveal whether they were male or female. Their baggy clothing obscured their figure, causing me to miss the initial movement.
But my eyes didn’t miss it. I stepped in further to evade the explosion that was likely to occur at my feet. I swung my sword from above.
Hurry up and reattach, ribs. I muttered in frustration as the attacker blocked my sword with their dagger.
“What the hell are you!”
The masked attacker shouted.
“I’m the husband of the woman you’re trying to kill!”
We shouted at each other in voices that, during body enhancement, would only sound like high-pitched squeaks to an ordinary person.
“I need you to die!”
With that childish declaration, I silently pushed my sword in, and when they lost their balance, I kicked them in the stomach.

Why does Erika have to be killed? I gritted my teeth at the absurdity of being told to die as if it were a matter of course. Perhaps because of that, I put a little too much force into the kick. The attacker let out a short scream and rolled further away than I expected.
I stepped in to finish them off.
“Damn it! I’ll stop being human!”
The moment the masked attacker shouted that, I was hit by a shock that drove into my side, and I was blown away, holding my breath. What hit me?
I spun twice on the ground. What the hell! What the hell! Ever since those six pitiful souls exploded, the situation has been changing rapidly, and I have no idea what's happening!
I dug my nails into the ground and forced myself to stand, struggling to keep my slipping body upright.
In that instant, I was left speechless, exposing myself as a fool who had lost his words in the midst of the fight.
I was left speechless by the face peering through the cracked mask, a face that was not human, and reflexively grimaced at the intense feeling of revulsion that surged within me.
Enough already, I thought sincerely. This is too much. It’s absolutely ridiculous.
As I tore at the clothes I was wearing, I realized the attacker was swelling up. It was not knowledge, but instinct that made me understand.
“What kind of joke is it that a human becomes a demon?”
I’ve never even heard such nonsense in tavern tales!
While I shouted that in my mind, I dealt with the attacker, who had transformed into a ridiculous two-legged horse with reptilian-like skin.

Demons──the enemies of humanity, alongside monsters. They appear from nowhere, wreak havoc, and cause damage. Often mistaken for monsters, they are entirely different beings. They instill a strong sense of revulsion in anyone who sees them.
That revulsion is enough to convince a human after just one sighting.
“This” is absolutely incompatible.
I dodged the thick arms that had grown as thick as an ogre’s and the tentacles that had likely punched me earlier, slashing with my sword.
The sensation was like cutting through a thick tree, making me grit my teeth. I regretted breaking my beloved sword just recently. I couldn’t fully trust the hastily prepared swords I had.

I had plenty to complain about the absurdity of a human becoming a demon, but more than that, I was anxious that my sword might break. After exchanging a few blows, the horse-faced demon suddenly ceased its attacks.
Before I could think “chance,” I was bewildered by the oddity. The horse-faced demon, with eyes that didn’t fit its horse-like face, was looking past me at something behind.
In that instant, I felt a chill. I sensed a hint of intelligence in the horse-faced demon’s eyes.
I wouldn’t say I was careless, but it was a fact that I was caught off guard. By the time I thought it was bad, it was too late.
I felt the sensation of tentacles wrapping around my ankle and realized I had made a huge mistake.
I was thrown. Well, I had thrown people around today, so it was only natural that I would be thrown at least once.
While thinking that, I yelled at the absurdity of a horse having tentacles and braced myself for the impact as I was slammed down. However, my back was met with an unexpectedly soft landing.
What the hell? Before I could think, a voice called out to me.
“Are you alright!? My lord!”
“Why are you still here?”
Complaints came out before I could express my gratitude for being saved.
“You two were just fighting at a ridiculous speed while I was running with all my might.”
I see, when using body enhancement, my sense of time gets all messed up.
“What was that about?”
“A former human demon.”
I answered Merseja’s question succinctly while regaining my stance, implying that he had seen it too.
“Thank goodness, I was sane after all.”
A smile involuntarily appeared on my face at Merseja’s lightheartedness. Speaking of which.
“Why are you stopping? If it’s a delay, I’ll handle it!”

The horse-faced demon was glaring at us with heavy breaths. Was it wary of Merseja, who was unharmed after I was thrown? No, that’s not it; it was healing. The cut I had inflicted on the demon was closing up. The act of waiting to heal while being cautious only made me feel more of that intelligence; a beast would run away when tired.
“Hey, while I was running at full speed, ‘for some reason,’ a hole appeared in the road, and when we passed through it, the axle got misaligned.”

Merseja’s kindness in not saying everything was touching. From now on, I’ll be careful not to create holes in the road. Public property is important; you shouldn’t break it. Well, it might have been caused by the explosion, but still.
Thinking about it, that was also my fault. Well, whatever, I’ll take responsibility.
“Well then, I’ll defeat it.”
“Can you?”
I shrugged at Merseja’s scrutinizing gaze. I didn’t dislike that kind of straightforwardness.
“Well, the sword might break, but if it does, I can just hit it.”
For some reason, Merseja sighed.
“As expected of the ‘Longdagger unworthy of his status.’”
What’s that supposed to mean? Before I could ask back, the horse-faced demon roared. The arm I had partially severed was healing cleanly. It had quite the regenerative ability.
But while it had the intelligence to wait for its injuries to heal, it seemed it lacked patience.
The horse-faced demon charged straight at me.
It was targeting the passenger car, not the driver’s seat. I still couldn’t believe it, but this demon had a semblance of intelligence. Yet, it was aiming for the passenger car, not me or Merseja.
In other words, its target was Erika Solnzali.
Anger ground my teeth.
Whoever it was, did they see Erika Solnzali as such an obstacle? After stealing her brilliant future, now they want to take her life too?
Don’t mess with me.
I won’t allow such absurdity.
The moment I thought that, I found myself leaping forward.
“I’ll crush this absurdity!”
And the moment I shouted, I regretted it.
I had charged straight in. Body enhancement magic doesn’t ignore physical laws. In other words, if I charged head-on at a massive demon, I would be blown away.
I should have just braced myself instead of charging; I regretted it while being thrown.
Well, it’s fine; I might crash into the carriage, but I won’t die. Next time, I’ll make sure to kill it.
In the brief moment before crashing into the carriage, I reached that conclusion.
──Then, my body braced for impact was stopped by a surprisingly gentle shock.
Before I could think about what had happened, I was captivated by the overflowing magic power in front of me. It was a beautiful golden magic that symbolized her nobility.
I had never met anyone who could see magic power besides myself. Therefore, I was the only one who knew this beautiful light of magic.
Noble golden magic──its owner.
Realizing my state, I forgot to breathe and turned my gaze.
“That was quite the good ‘retort,’ wasn’t it?”
Erika Solnzali, who had caught me with one arm, smiled.
“Yes, absurdities should be ‘crushed.’”
In an instant, the beautiful golden magic transformed into ferocity and blasted the charging horse-faced demon away. Remembering to breathe at last, I thought.
The return of the marquis daughter.
Would my heart stop? I seriously felt a sense of crisis as I escaped her arms and landed on the ground. My heart was pounding; would it burst? Would it explode?
“By the way, what on earth is going on? While I’m trying to regain my composure amidst all these difficulties, you’re making a ruckus.”
That cursed muttering was an effort to regain composure? I thought while calming my heart, which was racing like a monkey swinging a bell.
Erika Solnzali lightly stepped down from the carriage and swiftly brushed her disheveled hair with magic. My heart, which had begun to settle, was about to race again.
No, wait, calm down, this is getting out of hand.

I took a deep breath and took in her entire figure. Compared to her appearance at the academy, her travel attire lacked flashiness, but that simplicity only enhanced her beauty. Alright, Erika is beautiful; calm down.
Did she catch sight of me, staring dumbfounded, and Merseja, who was mesmerized? Erika Solnzali turned to us.
“Is that the coachman… and a bodyguard?”
I wanted to say, “I’m a classmate,” but I held back.
“Do you know where my sword is?”
“Unfortunately, your sword is among the luggage.”
I carefully turned the sword, stained with the blood of demons, toward her while being cautious.
“So please use mine.”
After comparing the hilt of the offered sword to my face, Erika Solnzali smiled brightly.
“I’ll gratefully accept it.”
Merseja, witnessing our exchange, raised a voice filled with anxiety, or rather, suspicion. Perhaps it was about professional ethics?
“My lord, are you sure about this?”
Though his words were lacking, I understood what Merseja meant.
For me, seeing Erika Solnzali holding a sword and standing firmly on the ground made me feel there was nothing to worry about.
But I understood that it was only natural for him to feel anxious if he didn’t know.

I told Erika Solnzali to leave the rest to her, and as I heard her say, “Leave it to me,” I sat down on the driver’s seat. By the way, I had cut off body enhancement before handing her the sword. Merseja looked at me with a face that seemed to want to say something.
“It’s alright, Merseja.”
At my words, Merseja looked at the back of the bodyguard who was walking away on her own.
“She is Erika Solnzali.”
Golden magic rose from her.
“There’s no way she can lose.”
“Isn’t that the person who was just spouting curses a moment ago?”
Merseja tilted his head and said.
“Well, there are times like that.”
“Is it only you who can accept that in this world?”
Merseja seemed to think for a moment but ultimately decided to watch her back like I did.
I saw the horse-faced demon, which had been down, stand up vigorously, and I sensed Merseja getting restless behind me, but I told him to calm down.
Could it be that even at rank six, he couldn’t see it? She was so obviously strong. Or was he being deceived by her beauty despite knowing?
If that’s the case, then Merseja’s aesthetic sense should be praised, as he understands that she is beautiful before she is strong.
Thinking that, I noticed Erika Solnzali laughing, even though I could only see her back, and I could tell her magic was shining joyfully.
She must be smiling.
Ah, what a pity; I should have followed her. If I had, I could have seen that profile again.
The horse-faced demon, now standing, seemed to prioritize targeting Erika Solnzali.
It didn’t even glance at us, who were wide open.
The horse-faced demon chose a straightforward charge as its attack method. While it had the intelligence to prioritize its target, it felt disjointed to choose a simple charge attack.
However, well, a charge utilizing its massive body isn’t a bad choice.
After all, simply dodging wouldn’t avoid attacks from the tentacles.

Avoiding the tentacles that sprouted from its back, I thought that eventually, I would be worn down by the difference in stamina. That horse-faced demon seemed confident in its stamina, given its horse head.
I looked at the horse-faced demon’s face, which seemed somewhat confident.
No, it’s truly foolish.
If the horse-faced demon had real intelligence, the first thing it should have done was run away. If it had chosen to flee at the first opportunity, it might have had a chance to escape.
Yet, here it was, trying to confront Erika Solnzali, and not just any Erika Solnzali, but one armed with a sword.
It had no trace of intelligence.
To me, who had cut off body enhancement, it only appeared to have vanished, but it seemed Merseja hadn’t cut off body enhancement, as he muttered in a dazed voice that it was too fast.
How much of her movements could he see as the horse-faced demon crumbled before him? I pondered that while calling out to Erika Solnzali.
“Be careful; that one has high regenerative abilities—”
Before I could finish my sentence, a pillar of fire erupted, and the pitiful horse-faced demon turned to ash.
As expected of Erika Solnzali, she was flawless.
The swirling flames created pillars of fire that blazed as if to scorch the heavens.
Against the backdrop of the rising flames, Erika Solnzali slowly approached us.

She brushed her red hair, which seemed to express her ferocity, and her eyes, filled with a strong will that could intimidate her opponent, narrowed with satisfaction, while her beautifully shaped lips curved into a gentle arc. The fact that she wore plain travel attire didn’t matter.
From any angle, she was undoubtedly the daughter of a high noble.
Unless you looked at the pillar of flames rising behind her.
Seeing that, Merseja said.
“You’ve really married an extraordinary wife.”
His voice carried a hint of exasperation.
But that’s right; I am, nominally, her husband.
When that fact was pointed out, I couldn’t help but let my cheeks relax.
Rather, I might have ended up with a rather creepy smile.
“I don’t think this is a time to be smiling, my lord.”
Merseja’s voice was now filled with an emotion that suggested he was truly exasperated.
……Was my smile really that creepy?
Killing someone, whether in self-defense or otherwise, requires a lot of cleanup afterward.
But in this case, I didn’t have much to worry about.

The horse-faced demon had turned to ash, leaving not even bones behind, and all the other attackers had exploded, leaving no trace. When I thought about it calmly, it was absurd; it was far too cheap to take a life.
As I fixed the misaligned axle of the carriage, Merseja returned, shaking his head after inspecting the scene.
In other words, there was no evidence leading to the identity of the attackers.
Merseja had picked up the sword used by the attackers, but he said it was unlikely to glean anything from it.

What I understood was that the enemy was well-prepared, capable of using body enhancement to its full extent, and had some mysterious means of turning humans into demons, something I had never heard of.
Honestly, I didn’t understand. However, I knew that staying still in this situation would be a bad move.
With body enhancement, I could have worked anywhere properly. Even a fallen adventurer would look for a more decent job.
As I recalled the eight people I had killed today, I finally managed to fit the misaligned axle back into place.
And so, we resumed our journey in the carriage.
“About that, isn’t it the other way around?”
Erika Solnzali said that while the door, which had been forcibly repaired with rope, rattled in the carriage.
By the way, the reason the carriage door was in such a state was that it had been kicked open to help me after I was blown away by the demon. Of course, it was Erika Solnzali who did that.
Setting aside the pitiful door, I raised an eyebrow, asking, “What do you mean?”
“Isn’t it that humans didn’t transform into demons, but rather demons transformed into humans?”

Ah, I see; that’s a perspective I hadn’t considered. While both are absurd tales I’ve never heard, psychologically, it’s easier to accept that demons transformed into humans than the other way around.
But that’s not right. I shook my head and replied.
“Unfortunately, Erika Solnzali, I think that’s probably incorrect. The attacker definitely said they would stop being human. If a demon had transformed into a human, they wouldn’t say that.”

Erika Solnzali thought for a moment and then said, “Yes, you’re right,” discarding her own opinion. It seemed her thought had arisen from the disbelief in the idea of a human becoming a demon, rather than from any certainty.
If I had a bit more trust, perhaps she wouldn’t have thought that way, but given that I was just a classmate whose face she barely remembered, it was probably impossible.
“So, Erika Solnzali, it’s difficult to even speculate on who attacked you based on the attackers. Do you have any ideas?”
Erika Solnzali smiled sadly at my words.
The fact that the Erika Solnzali I knew was wearing a weak smile unsettled me more than I expected. Perhaps sensing something from my expression, she gestured as if to interrupt my words.
In reality, I wanted to say something, but I couldn’t think of anything.
“Surely, I don’t have any idea that would lead to being exiled and having my life targeted.”
More than that, she changed her expression and said.
“Why do you keep calling me by my full name?”
Her expression seemed to hold a simple curiosity rather than reproach.
That face was both cute and beautiful.
As I was captivated by her, she seemed to recall something and furrowed her brow, looking displeased.
“By the way, I haven’t even asked for your name. Isn’t that rather rude to a lady?”
That remark was quite reasonable, but as someone who had been classmates for three years, I was honestly a bit hurt.

Well, regardless of whether it was a count’s house or a viscount’s house, whether it was rich or poor, the class difference was too great. I made sure not to show it on my face and placed my hand over my chest to apologize.
“I apologize for the delay, my lady. I am Shin Longdagger, the second son of a viscount family, barely scraping by as a member of the kingdom’s nobility.”
Hmm, why can’t I be serious until the end in situations like this?
Jokingly, I glanced up from my lowered head, and Erika Solnzali placed her finger on her well-shaped chin, seemingly deep in thought. It seemed my little jest was being overlooked.
“I thought you were an adventurer hired as a bodyguard… Longdagger, that name sounds familiar, or rather, if I look closely, I feel like I’ve seen it somewhere… where was it?”
Wasn’t that a bit too loud for a soliloquy? While I held back that thought, Erika Solnzali clapped her hands.
Hmm, cute.
